findings.title: View permission grants global group management
findings.body: This method treats either `view` or `manage` on the all-groups resource as `canManage()`. Callers use the no-argument check to authorize operations such as creating a top-level group (`requireManage()`), so an administrator granted only view access to all groups can perform management operations. Require the `manage` scope here; view-only access must not satisfy management checks.

findings.title: Group view filtering returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds `groupResource.getId()`, which is the authorization resource's internal ID, to the set used by user searches to filter users by their group IDs. The group resource's name is the actual group ID. Consequently users who should be visible through a group's `view-members` or `manage-members` permission are omitted from group-restricted user searches (and user counts); add the resource name/group ID instead.
